The government has allocated significant resources to this programme, recognising that breastfeeding provides substantial health benefits for both mothers and infants. We believe this initiative will help reduce health inequalities and give every child the best possible start in life. Further announcements will be made in the coming months as we finalise our plans, and we remain committed to working closely with stakeholders throughout this process.

"We will keep the contents under review and adapt these to meet the needs of babies and parents. This will certainly include considering what additional items could be provided to complement existing measures and support we provide to promote breastfeeding.

The pilot scheme, which launched in several regions last year, distributed informational materials and starter packs to new mothers. Early feedback indicated that while the resources were generally well-received, many parents expressed a desire for more practical support during the critical early weeks of breastfeeding. Officials are now examining options for expanding the program, potentially including improved access to lactation consultants and peer support networks. The government remains committed to increasing breastfeeding rates across the country, recognizing both the health benefits and the challenges many mothers face.

We will also ensure that any new provisions are delivered in a way that is accessible and practical for all families who need them. The pilot has demonstrated that targeted support can make a real difference in helping mothers feel more confident and informed about breastfeeding options. Our commitment is to continue working collaboratively with health professionals and community organizations to ensure this initiative reaches those who will benefit most. We believe this approach will help give every child the best possible start in life while respecting each family's individual choices.

pair.human_continuation: "The baby box is one of a range of measures we provide to give more children the best possible start in life. This includes providing free vitamins and healthy start vouchers for free milk, fruit and vegetables to pregnant women and families on low incomes with young children." The baby boxes, which were largely inspired by a scheme in Finland, have been broadly welcomed by health professionals and charities. The design for the box was unveiled in March, and features a forest fairytale design including Highland cows, squirrels and the Loch Ness Monster. The Scottish government, which is rolling out the boxes across Scotland after successful pilots in Clackmannanshire and Orkney, believes they will help tackle deprivation, improve health and support parents.
